timing.label: Objection 1 (data boundary)
timing.question: The control plane still sees our code, so what did we actually gain?

timing.label: Objection 2 (availability)
timing.question: What happens when the worker is down at 2 a.m.?

problem.quote: Execution moves into our VPC; inference does not.

approach.quote: a worker image we build and own, two workers on it

next_step.quote: Next action: create the Outpost with an admin.

must_mention.point: Commands, file edits and repo access run on Harbourline's worker in the VPC while inference and planning stay in Devin Cloud
must_mention.evidence_quote: every command, file edit and repo checkout runs on a Harbourline worker inside the VPC … Devin Cloud keeps planning and inference

must_mention.point: Worker started with devin worker start plus the outpost name and its token, the token shown once and kept in the secret manager
must_mention.evidence_quote: devin worker start, the outpost name harbourline-vpc and its token; the token is shown once, so it went straight into the secret manager

must_mention.point: One session per worker so two containers serve two sessions and the third waits under a banner rather than failing
must_mention.evidence_quote: one session per worker, so our two containers ran S1 and S2 and S3 waited under the banner

must_mention.point: Engineers reach the outpost through the organization default platform and the Slack bang command
must_mention.evidence_quote: type bang outpost in Slack, or do nothing once an admin makes it the organization default platform

must_mention.point: Image bakes in the repo with git, ffmpeg and Chrome via DEVIN_CHROME_PATH and grants no passwordless sudo
must_mention.evidence_quote: bakes in the repo with git, ffmpeg and Chrome through DEVIN_CHROME_PATH … grants no passwordless sudo

must_mention.point: Platform engineering rebuilds the image on a schedule and rolls one worker at a time
must_mention.evidence_quote: rebuild from the stable base every week … roll one worker at a time

must_mention.point: Which steps ran live and which only ran on the offline queue model
must_mention.evidence_quote: the image build ran here; worker registration, Slack and the default platform only ran on the offline queue model

accuracy.anchor: All seven points with names and numbers; the boundary is stated before the product (anchor: 27–30 = all points, precise).

structure.anchor: Every segment holds its skeleton; the update order held (anchor: 22–25 = order held throughout).

customer_relevance.anchor: Framed around the CISO's condition and her Friday deadline (anchor: 17–20 = customer outcome first).

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Every segment within ±5 s; one filler in 9.9 minutes, no long pauses (anchor: 13–15 = on target, fluent).

recovery.anchor: All three objections follow acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer (anchor: 9–10 = pattern held every time).

stems: "Execution moves; inference does not." — keep leading with the boundary.
"I saw this run live: … I rehearsed this offline: …" — you did this; keep it in every update.
"Two workers, two sessions; the third waits, it does not fail." — say the capacity number before the risk.
